title: quantization-debug-breadcrumbs-int8-fp8-bf16
content:
Context:
I've been following up on the NaN/quality regressions reported on int8 quantized model variants (primarily GPT-like causal models we onboarded last month). This doc is a running scratchpad of commands, outputs, hypotheses and quick experiments I tried while pairing with Ethan and Rina. Not polished - mostly breadcrumbs for the next debugging session and for linking to the incident ticket (INF-523).

Symptoms observed:
- Intermittent NaNs during sampling with int8 quantized checkpoints (fp8 variants show lower frequency but occasional numerical instability).
- Quality regressions on some prompts (hallucinations and broken completions) when using per-channel symmetric int8 quantization with outlier folding turned on.
- Some model runs show hidden state activations contain NaN starting at layer 10-ish (varies).

Environment / setup notes:
- Model: community/gpt-large-like (architecture: 32 layers, rotary embeddings, flash attention).
- Baseline fp16 (bfloat16 training checkpoint): good. Quantization recipes tried: symmetric per-channel int8, asymmetric per-tensor int8, per-channel fp8 (E4M3), bf16 fallback.
- Runtime: inference-runtime v2.3.1 (local dev container), CUDA 12.1, cuBLAS/cuDNN default. Using Redwood serving dev image: redwood-dev/inference:local-2026-01.
- Tools: quantize.py (internal), inspect_activations.py (hooked into the runtime via kv-cache dump), small eval harness (eval/qual_test.py).

Quick commands and outputs (timestamps):
1) Reproduce minimal NaN (2026-01-16 09:12)
$ python -m inference_runtime.run --model ./models/gpt-large-fp16 --quant int8 --prompt "Write a short email about Q1 results" --max-tokens 64
...
Runtime error: nan encountered in hidden state at layer 12 token 7
Traceback (most recent calls):
  File "/app/inference_runtime/runner.py", line 241, in generate
    out = self.step(inputs)
  File "/app/inference_runtime/engine/int8_kernels.py", line 98, in step
    x = fused_attention(x, ... )
  File "/app/inference_runtime/utils/numeric_checks.py", line 22, in check_nan
    raise NumericError("NaN in tensor: hidden_states layer 12")
NumericError: NaN in tensor: hidden_states layer 12

2) Quick activation dump (2026-01-16 09:16)
$ python inspect_activations.py --model-dir ./models/gpt-large-int8-debug --dump-layers 8-14 --prompt-file examples/prompts.txt
Output (layer 11): mean=0.0234 std=0.19 max=1.3e+02 min=-1.2e+02 nonfinite_count=0
Output (layer 12): mean=nan std=nan max=nan min=nan nonfinite_count=1.2e+03
Note: nonfinite_count corresponds to number of NaNs/inf in that layer activation tensor.

3) Sanity check with fp16 run (2026-01-16 09:25)
$ python -m inference_runtime.run --model ./models/gpt-large-fp16 --prompt "same prompt"
Success: no NaNs, outputs look normal.

Hypotheses at this point:
- Hypothesis A: Quantization scales for certain channels are badly estimated due to outliers not captured in calibration dataset (per-channel scales blowing up -> overflow/inf -> NaN after some ops).
- Hypothesis B: Kernel numeric path (fusion of attention + softmax + dropout) with int8 path has a bug causing division by zero or accumulation overflow in the softmax exponent when input ranges are large.
- Hypothesis C: KV cache or rotary angle scaling mismatch between quantized and non-quantized paths leading to huge exponent values in attention scores.

What I tried (fast experiments):
- Re-ran calibration with extended dataset (added 10k more tokens from conversational logs) -> created new scale tables. Result: reduced NaN frequency by ~40% but not eliminated.
- Switched to asymmetric per-tensor int8 (scale + zero_point) -> NaNs reduced but quality worse on some prompts.
- Disabled outlier folding in quantizer (outlier folding: moving extreme weight values into fp16 side-channels). Outcome: NaNs increased; suggests outlier folding wasn't the root cause but may mask some instability.
- Run with fp8 (E4M3) per-channel quantization: more stable than int8 in these cases, but occasional NaN remains for long prompts (length > 200).
- Added numeric checks after linear layers to log max/mean/finite counts (see inspect_activations.py). Observed the first NaN appears immediately after the attention matmul that computes attention scores (Q*K^T) before softmax in many runs.

Detailed debug trace (reconstructed):
- Step n: compute Q (quantized dequant -> matmul) -> Q has large entries (max ~1e3) in some channels
- Compute scores = Q @ K^T / sqrt(dk) -> scores show very large positive values in some rows (1e4), then softmax exponent exp(scores) -> inf -> normalized -> NaN in attention output.

Quick check: Are scales being applied before matmul?
- Found that in the int8 fused kernel we dequantize on the fly with scale factors per-channel, but there was a misplaced reduce that computed per-tensor scale for K but per-channel for Q -> mismatch. This looks like a plausible bug (fixed in local patch int8-kernel-fix-2026-01).

Patch applied (2026-01-18):
- Fix: ensure both Q and K use consistent per-channel scale dimensions when reconstructing float tensors for matmul. Also added clamp on reconstructed floats to [-1e3, 1e3] as a temporary guard.
- Re-run full harness: NaNs eliminated in most cases; however, still saw NaN on long-prompt stress test in 2/100 runs (reproducible with specific prompt id #473 from eval set).

New lead: softmax numerics on long sequences
- For the failing prompt, scores max ~1e5 (after clamp, still high) which causes exp overflow. Why are scores that high after clamp? That indicates either clamp value too permissive or input accumulations still blow up because of large kv cache values.
- Investigated rotary embeddings: found rotation factors applied in quantized path were using truncated cosine lookup table (int16) with insufficient precision causing phase mismatch -> small drift accumulates across tokens -> occasionally leads to constructive interference in attention -> large scores.

Commands for rotary test (2026-01-20):
$ python -c "from inspect_rotary import compare_tables; print(compare_tables(\"models/gpt-large-fp16\", \"models/gpt-large-int8\"))"
Output: max_delta=6.4e-3 mean_delta=1.8e-3
We expect smaller delta (1e-6 - 1e-4). This is a smoking gun for accumulation error. Fix applied: increase rotary table precision and use float32 intermediate in quantized path.

Post-rotary fix (2026-01-22):
- NaNs dropped to 0 in 1000-run stress test for the previously failing prompt set.
- Quality: int8 outputs now visually closer to fp16 for short and medium prompts. Some remaining quality gap for long prompts.

Other notes / small experiments: 
- Reproduced a small failure when using per-tensor symmetric quantization + fused attention kernel that uses integer GEMM (int8->int32 accum). There was an unchecked int32 overflow possibility for sequence lengths > 512 when values were large. Added 64-bit accum fallback for long sequences in the runtime (configurable via env INFER_ACCUM_TYPE=int64).
- When switching accum to int64, throughput drops ~8% on A100 but stability improves. Might be acceptable as a safety mode for enterprise customers with long context windows.

Open action items / next steps:
- (Priority) Add regression test to eval harness that runs the two failing prompts (ids 473, 589) across quantization recipes (int8, fp8, bf16) and asserts no NaNs and KL-divergence < threshold vs fp16 baseline.
- (Engineering) Formalize per-channel scale agreement: add unit tests for scale broadcast shapes for all kernels (attention matmul, feedforward linear).
- (Perf) Evaluate possibility of dynamic clamp scaling instead of fixed clamp to reduce perf impact while avoiding exp overflow.
- (Product) Propose guard rails in Redwood Console: per-request fallback to bf16 if numeric instability detected (numeric watchdog that checks nonfinite counts in first N tokens and triggers fallback).
- (Benchmark) Re-run unit-cost evaluation with int64 accum fallback to measure real world cost impact and offer as an opt-in.

Misc debugging notes (random bits):
- Found a Slack convo: slack:#serving-runtime thread "int8 NaN surge" (link in linked_artifacts) with useful reproducer prompt.
- Jira INF-523 updated with the rotary fix patch and notes.
- See GH PR 142 for int8 kernel shape fix + tests.

If pairing later, bring laptop with nvprof enabled and we can run the failing prompt under nvprof to inspect kernel outputs per layer. Also want to run with NUMPY_WARN=error to see if any numpy ops produce warnings in calibration pipeline.

TODO (short):
- [ ] Add regression tests for prompts 473/589 (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Add unit tests for scale broadcast shapes (owner: Rina)
- [ ] Create flag INFER_ACCUM_TYPE and test perf impact across GPUs (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Draft Redwood Console spec for numeric watchdog (owner: product)
short_description: Scratchpad: debugging NaNs and quality regressions for int8/fp8/bf16 quantized inference - commands tried, traces, hypotheses, and next steps
